title: Imaging of Joint Response to Physiological Stress with Age, Sex and in Osteoarthritis
text:
Osteoarthritis (OA) is a leading cause of pain, reduced joint function, and disability, that reduces productivity and
quality of life at tremendous cost to society. Diagnostic imaging of OA is limited by methods that largely assess
late-stage disease changes or require longitudinal scanning and are performed in a static fashion that has limited
sensitivity to joint function in response to loading from everyday tasks such as walking or climbing stairs. This
work aims to develop a novel imaging “stress test”, based on [18F]NaF PET-MRI, that is able to evaluate at a
single time point, both the function of the whole-joint unit from physiological joint loading and multiple early
markers of OA.

title: Mapping the Causal Genetic-Imaging-Clinical Pathway for Alzheimer's Disease
text:
This research targets at developing novel statistical tools for jointly analyzing the human brain functional
activity and genetic information contained in biomedical datasets, and boosting the understanding of the
human functional connectivity patterns, their genetic/genomic markers and their causal pathway for the
Alzheimer’s disease across different scales. Our proposed methods will offer in-depth investigation of human
functional connectivity variations that may contribute to clinical, behavioral and cognitive outcomes. We expect
the accomplishments from this project to have significant impact in the understanding of the causal pathways
of the Alzheimer’s disease.

title: Lipid Nanoparticle Vector for Prenatal Gene Therapy Treatment of Apert Syndrome
text:
Apert Syndrome (AS) is a genetic disorder caused by mutations in fibroblast growth factor receptor-2 (FGFR-2)
and characterized by severe congenital deformities of the craniofacial skeleton, resulting in lifelong challenges
for affected children. Since the only treatment for AS is postnatal reconstructive surgery which, despite state-
of-the-art care, results in severe residual deformity, the proposed research plan is to develop gene editing and
suppression modalities delivered by lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) that are capable of targeting AS mutations and
to use them to understand how manipulation of pathophysiological FGFR-2 signaling can affect human bone
differentiation phenotypes in cells from AS patients. The work will also evaluate LNPs as vectors to deliver
nucleic acid-based therapies to bone progenitor cells during fetal development, paving the way for in utero
delivery of genetic therapies for developmental correction of structural deformities in AS and other craniofacial
disorders.

title: Transplant Pathology and Tissue Imaging Core B
text: For this P01, The Transplant Pathology, Tissue Imaging, Proteomic and Transcriptomics Core (Core B) will play a critical and well-integrated scientific role in supporting the two Projects, with a strong emphasis on the central focus of the Program, that concerns innovative approaches to promote regulatory immune cell function, extend renal allograft survival and allow IS drug withdrawal in rhesus macaques. Project 1 (Thomson) will focus on innovative approaches to promote regulatory dendritic cell (DCreg) function, whereas Project 2 (Ezzelarab) will extend current studies on the potential of novel anti-inflammatory agents to enhance regulatory T cell (Treg) function, extend graft survival and allow IS drug withdrawal in monkeys receiving a similar baseline IS regimen to those in Project 1. Core B will also work in close conjunction with Core A (Administration, Biostatistics and Bioinformatics) and Core C (Nanotechnology) to optimize Program integration and synergy and to achieve the overall objectives of the Research Program. The Specific Aims of Core B are to: Prepare, store, and optimally analyze tissue biopsies using routine histopathologic and protein localization techniques through implementation of digital quantitation of proteins and mRNA in specific regions of interest. 2. Evaluate and report the routine histopathologic diagnoses, recognize trends, and propose subsequent direction for future studies using a variety of innovative analytic techniques, including innovative assessment of sub- pathological rejection (as defined by enhanced colonization of the allograft by effector cells not detectable by routine light microscopy and potential immune synapse formation in kidney allografts) as predictors of safe withdrawal of immunosuppression. 3. Provide technical and professional expertise in the design and implementation of the tissue diagnostic strategies, including digital imaging, image analysis (including tracking of CARTregs), and NGP as needed. 4. Prioritize scheduling of samples, based on histopathological data, in consultation with the PLs and in relation to meeting the objectives of the Research Program.

title: Autologous chimeric antigen receptor engineered T cell immunotherapy for desensitization in patients awaiting kidney transplantation
text:
Anti-HLA antibodies present a formidable barrier to achieving a successful kidney transplant in
patient with end-stage renal failure. Many approaches have failed to reduce the level of anti-HLA
antibodies. This proposal leverages a novel form of engineered T cell therapy to eradicate the
cells responsible for producing these antibodies in patients on the kidney waiting list.

title: Integrated Research Training on Vector Borne Diseases in Pakistan: Vector Biology, Virology and Disease Epidemiology.
text: This D43 International Research Training Grant award will develop an Integrated Interdisciplinary VBD Research Training Program in which researchers will work under the close supervision of a Transdisciplinary Research Advisory Committee that will ensure learning through the integration of multidisciplinary methods and concepts and help researchers develop integrated research strategies. This program will foster the use of metagenomic, bioinformatics, mathematical modelling, implementation science, and advanced immunological techniques to examine relationships between pathogens, vectors, hosts, and their environments. This program will also develop a transdisciplinary VBD Professionals’ Learning Network in Pakistan that will bring frontline researchers across disciplines to engage and exchange VBD-linked information using a One Health

title: Biomedical Informatics and Data Science Training at Yale
text: Biomedical Informatics focuses on the creative use of computers in support of clinical medicine, biomedical research, and medical education, and Biomedical Data Science is a field concerned with analyzing and deriving knowledge from increasingly large data sets that are being collected across every field of clinical medicine and the biosciences. The goal of Yale's Biomedical Informatics and Data Science training program is to provide graduate students and postdoctoral fellows with coursework and experience that will allow them to pursue productive research careers in Biomedical Informatics and Data Science broadly defined. 1

title: Mechanisms of JAG1-mediated immune suppression in the pancreatic cancer microenvironment
text:
Targeting signals integral to pancreatic cancer suppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) is an unmet need
and an essential goal for achieving complete and durable responses to current therapy including immunotherapy.
Here, we investigate a novel mechanism by which JAG1, a pancreatic cancer worse prognostic marker, regulates
the suppressive TME by impairing the anti-tumor immune response of immune cell infiltration, metabolic fitness,
and function. The overarching goal of this study is to test if targeting JAG1 could overcome pancreatic cancer
immunotherapy-resistance and to reinvigorate anti-tumor response.

title: Data Harmonization and Analysis Core
text: DATA HARMONIZATION AND ANALYSIS CORE In the last six years, the United States has witnessed enormous changes concerning the public acceptance of cannabis. In short, cannabis and hemp products are widely available in North America. A critical but unexplored aspect of cannabis legalization is the extent to which the health effects of cannabis products depend on the ratio of THC and CBD, how endocannabinoids may mediate these effects, and how these effects may vary across the lifespan. The endocannabinoid system (ECS), which is a combination of CB1 and CB2 receptors as well as a number of endogenous ligands (2-AG, AEA) and lipid mediators, changes dramatically over the lifespan and likely mediates the effects of cannabinoids on the brain and immune system. To understand the neurocognitive and health effects of THC and CBD, it is imperative to understand their effects on the ECS. The Data Harmonization and Analysis Core (DHAC) will harmonize the clinical data, neurocognitive data, and the measurement of THC, CBD, metabolites, and endocannabinoids in blood to understand how THC and CBD influence the ECS and how changes in the ECS may mediate the effects of THC and CBD across the lifespan. To that end, the DHAC will develop and deploy a system for the support of the data collection, data harmonization, data analysis and data sharing needs of the RM-CRC (Aim 1). The DHAC will also harmonize clinical, cannabinoid and metabolite data, endocannabinoid and lipid mediator data from seven existing R01s (n=1359) in order to enable advanced machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) analyses to identify a panel of analytes that will be examined broadly in the RM-CRC and beyond (Aim 2). The DHAC will also conduct specialized analyses of the harmonized P50 project data to construct and test cross- groups simultaneous structural equation models describing how the effects of THC and CBD on the ECS and the association with downstream neurocognitive and clinical variables change across the lifespan (Aim 3). Finally, the DHAC will conduct analyses of ABCD data to examine the effects of THC and CBD in adolescents and to determine if ECS analytes are related to trajectory of brain development and substance use and provide a platform for future ML analyses of harmonized neuroimaging, clinical, and biological data to determine how THC and CBD and the ECS are associated with changes in structural and functional measures of connectivity in the brain (Aim 4).

title: Unanswered AAV Biology and Genome Fate Modulation Across Viral and Synthetic Substrates
text:
Charactering episomes from AAV-treated human decedents and comparative analyses with
already generated mouse data will identify conserved or different “signatures” associated
with persistence. These ﬁndings will provide AAV biology knowledge to guide ITR engineering
for lowering dose requirements and enable cross-platform episome engineering for nonviral
synthetic substrates.

title: Sleep and Circadian Timing Irregularities as Short-term Risk Factors for Adolescent Suicide: An Intensive Longitudinal Study
text:
Suicide is a leading cause of death among adolescents, and disrupted sleep and circadian rhythms are
promising, yet underexplored, contributors to short-term suicide risk. This study will be the first to examine a
biological indicator of endogenous circadian timing in relation to suicidal thoughts and behaviors, facilitating the
investigation into whether sleep behaviors, circadian timing, and their alignment increase short-term risk for
suicide. This proposal has both scientific and clinical significance because findings from this research may
inform real-time, sleep- and chronotherapy-based interventions to reduce suicide risk in youth.

title: Multi-modal machine learning to guide adjuvant therapy in surgically resectable colorectal cancer
text:
Development of the models proposed in this application will contribute to the unmet need for accurate, broadly
accessible stratification tools to enhance precision medicine for colorectal cancer (CRC). Public availability of
our models and de-identified dataset will enhance future machine learning–based CRC research by other
investigators. Finally, these resources and models are readily extendable to other cancer types.

title: miR-29: A brain homeostasis molecule for Alzheimer’s disease prevention
text:
The mature brain has a remarkable ability to maintain long-term homeostasis throughout adulthood. We have
identified a key molecule, called miR-29, which has an essential function in maintaining the mature brain
during normal healthy aging. The experiments we propose focus on investigating the mechanisms of action of
miR-29 in the adult brain as well as test its therapeutic efficacy in models of Alzheimer’s Disease.

title: Pediatric Cardiopulmonary MRI using RF Navigators and High Dimensional Deep Learning
text:
Pediatric cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, including congenital heart diseases, lung disease of
prematurity, and cystic fibrosis, require multiple imaging studies to evaluate the cardiovascular and pulmonary
systems, but this is currently done in separate scans that are very long and labor intensive. This project aims to
develop MRI methods for integrated cardiopulmonary evaluation in pediatrics, including advances in MRI
hardware, data acquisition, and image reconstruction, that will provide anatomical and functional information in
a single, rapid scan. This will improve the diagnosis, treatment selection, and monitoring of cardiopulmonary
diseases in pediatrics, and also will improve our fundamental understanding of the interaction between the
cardiovascular and pulmonary systems, all without the use of ionizing radiation.

title: Optimizing Ultrasensitive DNA methylation detection for lung cancer and other malignancies
text:
This proposal for a Biomarker Characterization Center seeks to improve upon the management
of lung cancer and other malignancies through detection of tumor specific abnormal DNA
methylation in plasma. The Biomarker Development Lab will discover new loci with a high
prevalence of cancer specific methylation in lung cancer and others, and develop new and more
sensitive methods of detection. These approaches will be transferred to the Biomarker
Reference Lab for testing in a clinical setting, and operations of these two components and their
communication facilitated by the Administrative Core.

title: Investigating mitochondrial dysfunction in high-risk prostate cancer
text:
Prostate cancer is the second-leading cause of cancer-related deaths in men in the United States,
governed by profound disparities in disease aggressiveness, incidence, and mortality. This proposal will perform
correlative studies in novel preclinical models and high-risk human prostate cancer to identify previously
unrecognized mitochondrial genomic and functional alterations in aggressive prostate cancer. These studies will
ultimately result in new precision prostate cancer interceptions that can potentially improve the survival and
reduce morbidity in high-risk populations.

title: Genetic Variants of Immune Dysregulation and Thrombotic Microangiopathy in Severe Pediatric Sepsis Induced Organ Dysfunction
text:
While risk for severe infection is known to have a heritable component with offspring of parents
who died from infection at a young age having a 6-fold increase in their risk of death from
infection, the contributing genetic factors remain unknown. Using whole exome sequencing, this
project aims to identify genetic sites of immune variation that associate with the development of
sepsis-associated thrombotic microangiopathy and hyperinflammation, phenotypes at high-risk
of poor sepsis outcome. This effort will identify specific genotypes that convey risk for poor
outcome and may identify outcome-associated mechanisms as potential future therapeutic
targets in severe pediatric sepsis.

title: Population Sciences
text: The goal of the Population Sciences Program (PS) of the Stanford Cancer Institute (SCI) is to conduct high- impact transdisciplinary and translational research across the cancer continuum aimed at improving detection through screening, reducing cancer incidence, morbidity and mortality, and improving cancer outcomes. The PS achieves this goal by promoting and facilitating innovative multidisciplinary observational and interventional research on cancer that will impact public health and guide clinical practice and health policy. PS members are nationally and internationally recognized clinical and population scientists with a broad range of unique strengths in epidemiology, genetics, quantitative modeling, bioinformatics, use of novel technologies, behavioral science, lifestyle (physical activity, diet, tobacco control, sleep), and clinical and palliative care interventional trials, and community health and prevention research. The program’s overarching research priorities include reducing the cancer burden in the population of SCI’s catchment area. PS members’ research addresses the following Specific Aims: Aim 1: Conduct research on cancer etiology, risk prediction, screening, and genetic testing; Aim 2: Investigate the impact of cancer treatment and prognostic factors on outcomes; and Aim 3: Conduct intervention research to reduce cancer risks and improve outcomes. The PS has 39 members, of whom 31 are supported by peer-reviewed funding totaling $14.0M, including $7.4M from the NCI, $5.0M other cancer-relevant NIH support, and $1.6M from other peer-reviewed support. During the current funding period, PS members published 1,130 peer-reviewed manuscripts. Of these, 22% are intra- programmatic, 23% are inter-programmatic, 96% are multi-institutional, and 18% are in journals with an impact factor of 10 or higher. Support from the SCI has been instrumental in promoting both intra- and inter- programmatic collaborations of PS members, recruiting new faculty members, and enabling preliminary research through innovation grants that lead to externally funded projects. PS members also strive to train the next generation of cancer prevention researchers. In the future, the PS will further expand and focus on research in genetic risk profiling and assessment, outcomes and survivorship research across the life course, and health services and implementation science, and will develop and submit a T32 training grant in genetic epidemiology and population sciences.

title: Community-driven drug prevention implementation strategies for Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander youth in rural Hawai'i
text: This high-risk, high-reward proposal challenges the typical scientific paradigm through innovative approaches in youth substance use prevention in rural geographic settings. Implementation science and participatory methods will balance power, ownership, and responsibility between university researchers and local communities to actively promote adoption and sustainment of school-based substance use prevention. Community-led innovation tournaments and ecological momentary assessment will produce new generalizable findings for other populations with historically limited access to services, promoting the spread and reach of school-based substance use prevention.

title: FIGOR: Fellowship In Genomics Outcomes Research
text: The purpose of the Fellowship In Genomics Outcomes Research (FIGOR) is for Genetic Counselor Scholars (GCS) to experience mentored research in a highly collaborative and supportive environment with 50% effort protected time for 24 months. GCS will gain experience in translational research skills in the areas of genomic sciences and genomic medicine, as well as the ethical, legal and social implications of these areas. The experience will simultaneously educate genetic counselors and scientists in the value of collaboration to maximize and broaden the impact of translational research.
